content: Flucytosine is a medication used to treat severe fungal infections within the body. It belongs to a class of drugs known as antifungal agents and is often prescribed in combination with other medications to enhance its effectiveness. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your physician, typically four times a day (every six hours). To minimize stomach upset, avoid swallowing all capsules for a single dose at once. Instead, space them out as instructed. For optimal efficacy, maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body by taking it at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow the infection to return. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. Refer to the usage instructions for tips on reducing stomach upset. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your physician for guidance. Precautions: Before starting flucytosine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Flucytosine can increase your susceptibility to infections or exacerbate existing infections. Avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections (e.g., chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, flu). Notify your healthcare provider that you are taking flucytosine before receiving any immunizations or vaccinations. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not recommended during the first three months of pregnancy due to potential harm to the unborn baby. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Flucytosine may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., serum creatinine), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Monitoring: Regular laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney and liver function, blood cell counts, blood mineral levels) should be conducted while taking this medication. Attend all scheduled medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: Use this medication with caution if you have kidney problems, as flucytosine may impair kidney function and cause liver issues. This medication may also reduce bone marrow function, potentially leading to a decrease in red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. This can result in anemia, reduced ability to fight infections, and bleeding problems. Your doctor will monitor your kidney, liver, and blood test results and adjust your treatment to minimize these risks.
